q1.label: Are the image quality and view adequate to judge the answer?
q1.help: Judge only image quality and view.

option_notes.yes: good enough to judge the whole answer.
option_notes.partly: good enough for only part of the answer (for example, part of the structure is out of view). Judge only that part.
option_notes.no: the image quality or view is too poor to judge any part of the answer. This ends the record.

q2.label: Is the question–answer pair itself valid? Tick all that apply.
q2.help: Recorded separately from Q1; continue to Q3–Q4 even if not valid.

options.unanswerable: Question cannot be answered from the image and the information in the question
options.off_topic: Answer does not address the question

q3.label: Is the answer accurate? Choose one.
q3.help:
If there is more than one kind of problem, choose only the most serious: Wrong > Under-stated > Over-stated. Record the others in the optional error types (E1–E7), where you can tick several (tricky case 4).
Q3 is about the words only; a mask on the wrong structure is recorded in Q4. Use the standard lexicon (BI-RADS, TI-RADS) where one exists.

option_notes.accurate: nothing is wrong, over-stated or missing.
option_notes.wrong: something stated is incorrect: a finding that is not in the image, the location or side, the description or diagnosis, or a measurement or count.
option_notes.over_stated: the answer goes beyond the evidence (neither the image nor the question supports it), or is more certain than the evidence allows; for example "biopsy-proven" when the question gives no pathology, or "malignant" where only suspicious features are seen. Citing history or pathology that the question itself provides is not over-stated.
option_notes.under_stated: an important finding within the question's scope is missing (tricky case 1).

q4.label: Records with a mask only: do the question, the answer text and the mask point to the same target?
q4.help: Check only that they refer to the same target; no pixel-level check of the outline is needed. A mask on the wrong structure is recorded here only (Q4 = "No"), not in Q3. With several masks, choose No if any one of them does not point to the same target, and say in the case note which one (for example Mask 2).

optional.intro: These help us describe the errors but do not change the three outcome classes. Leave them blank if you are short of time.

error_types.label: Error type (E1–E7)
error_types.help: When Q3 is Wrong, Over-stated or Under-stated, you can add the error types (see Error types), ticking as many as apply, including those of less serious problems you did not choose in Q3: Wrong = E1, E3, E4, E6; Over-stated = E5, E7; Under-stated = E2.

significance.label: Clinical significance
significance.help: Likely significant = likely to change interpretation, management or triage (tricky case 3). Use "Not applicable (phantom)" only for phantom images; phantom images are still judged for accuracy in Q3 as usual (tricky case 9).

quote.label: Quoted words
quote.help: When you tick Over-stated, quoting the words is recommended but not required.

note.label: Case note
note.help: Use it for any problem that the questions above do not cover. For records outside your experience, write "needs specialist review" in the note.
